scope: Independent adjudication against the original base-game multiplayer rules and mandatory two-player House Hagal rules. Only the assigned case file, extracted rules text, and original rules PDF were read as task evidence. Support metadata was not used to determine grades.

adjudications.reason: The answer covers occupied-space redraws, immediate reshuffling, replacing normal space costs/effects with card effects, recruitment, direct deployment on Combat spaces, and the additional deployment of up to two garrison troops. It leaves the explicitly requested Harvest Spice bonus procedure unresolved: when House Hagal harvests a space, all bonus spice on that space must be removed and returned to the bank in a two-player game. Describing how a space is selected by its bonus does not state or imply clearing that bonus. This is a material omission, rather than an asserted wrong rule. The supplied rulebook delegates Harvest Spice selection details to the card; the more detailed selection and conditional two-space wording in the answer is not independently established by the supplied rulebook text, and is not treated as a proven contradiction.
adjudications.missing_material_procedure: Remove any bonus spice from the harvested space and return it to the bank; House Hagal does not collect it.

sources.section: House Hagal Cards — Solo & Two-Player Games / Agents
sources.supports: Occupied-space redraw, immediate reshuffle, card effects instead of normal space costs/effects, troop recruitment and deployment.
Follow the card instructions; remove any bonus spice when a Rival harvests; return it to the bank in a two-player game.
House Hagal does not collect resources.

adjudications.reason: The answer correctly gives two strength per Conflict troop plus the revealed card's swords, requires a Conflict troop for the Combat bonus, permits human Combat Intrigue afterward, retains House Hagal's competitive rank without awarding it rewards, removes the human Control marker without replacing it when House Hagal wins that space, and distinguishes a human tie for second from ordinary third place. However, its exact phrase 'reveal Hagal cards until non-Reshuffle' specifies which card ultimately provides swords and that another card must be revealed; it does not specify rebuilding and shuffling the deck when the Reshuffle card appears. The named card is used only as the stopping-condition exclusion, without an instruction to resolve that card. Continuing through the existing deck and shuffling before the next reveal both satisfy the literal wording, so the required intervening shuffle cannot be inferred uniquely. Page 19 explicitly requires reshuffling the deck and then revealing again. Because that omitted operation changes the deck from which the Combat bonus is drawn, it is a material unresolved part of the requested strength procedure. The answer does not explicitly prohibit reshuffling, so this is an omission and merits partial rather than incorrect. No procedure from another answer is imported.

sources.section: Player Turn — Reveal Turn / Set Strength
sources.supports: Each troop in the Conflict contributes two strength; at least one Conflict troop is required for any strength.

sources.section: House Hagal Cards — Solo & Two-Player Games / Combat
sources.supports: At Combat start, a Rival with at least one Conflict troop gets a revealed-card sword bonus; revealing Reshuffle requires reshuffling the deck and then revealing again; humans may then play Combat Intrigue.
House Hagal competes in Conflicts but earns no rewards, cannot claim control, and removes the current player's Control marker when it wins that space.

sources.section: Phase 3: Combat / Resolve Combat and Ties
sources.supports: Rewards follow strength rank; ordinary third-place reward exists only in four-player games; players tied for second each receive the third reward.

adjudications.missing_material_procedure: When the Reshuffle card is revealed for the Combat bonus, reshuffle the House Hagal deck before revealing the next card.
